questions.prompt: On this T2-weighted MRI of the pelvis, click the urinary bladder.
questions.hint: The midline hollow organ behind the pubic bones.
questions.explain: The urinary bladder is the midline pelvic reservoir for urine. On T2 the urine is bright, contrasting with the dark muscular wall.

questions.prompt: On this T2-weighted MRI of the pelvis, click the prostate.
questions.hint: A walnut-sized gland just below the bladder, in front of the rectum.
questions.explain: The prostate surrounds the proximal urethra below the bladder neck. On T2 the peripheral zone is bright and the central gland is darker and more heterogeneous.

questions.prompt: On this T2-weighted MRI of the pelvis, click the femur.
questions.hint: The long bone of the thigh whose rounded head fits into the pelvis.
questions.explain: The femur is the longest bone, and its head articulates with the acetabulum. On T2 the marrow is intermediate to bright and the cortex is dark.

questions.prompt: On this T2-weighted MRI of the pelvis, click the gluteus maximus.
questions.hint: The largest, most superficial buttock muscle.
questions.explain: Gluteus maximus is the main extensor of the hip and forms the bulk of the buttock. On T2 muscle is darker than fat and fluid, with fine bright fat striations.

questions.prompt: A 30-year-old man has fever, severe hip pain and refuses to bear weight on the left leg, and septic arthritis is suspected. On this T2-weighted MRI, click the bone that forms the socket of this joint.
questions.hint: The large pelvic bone that contains the acetabulum.
questions.explain: The acetabulum of the hip bone forms the socket of the hip joint, where infection produces a joint effusion. On T2 the effusion appears bright within the joint space.

questions.prompt: A 65-year-old woman has left lower abdominal pain, fever and altered bowel habit, and diverticulitis is suspected. On this T2-weighted MRI, click the part of the bowel most likely to be inflamed.
questions.hint: It frames the small bowel and passes down the left side of the pelvis.
questions.explain: Diverticulitis involves inflamed outpouchings of the sigmoid colon, with wall thickening and pericolic fat stranding. On T2 the thickened wall and surrounding fluid are bright.
